extracted.intended_audience: advanced mathematics students and researchers studying porisms and analytic/coordinate geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Algebraic/coordinate-method solution techniques and methodological principles for porisms (classical geometric propositions) — how to set up coordinates, introduce parameters, form porismatic equations, and extract conditional relations. Focused on analytic manipulation (elimination, equating coefficients) and sign/notation conventions used in these investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose coordinate axes to exploit symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer the system to rectangular co-ordinates originating at A, and such that the axis of x shall bisect the given angle BAC; and, denote by K the semi-angles BAX, CAX, and by Φ the porismatic point H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select axes (for example, let one axis bisect a given angle or take given lines as axes) so that the equations of given lines/circles become simpler and symmetry is exploited. Several alternatives of axis choice are explicitly recommended later (see methods (1)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express geometric objects in coordinates and derive algebraic equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Denote by h, k the co-ordinates of the centre of the variable circle through A and H, we shall have [algebraic equations of circle]. Also the equations of the lines AB, AC, are respectively y = x tan K, and y = -x tan K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write equations of lines, circles, intersections etc. in coordinate form; find intersection abscissas/ordinates by substitution; express lengths (AD, AE, BD, CE, etc.) algebraically in terms of coordinates to form the porismatic relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an equation must hold for arbitrary parameter, equate coefficients to zero
rubrics_metrics.description: Equating the coefficients in reference to the arbitrary quantity h, to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an equation contains an indeterminate/arbitrary quantity (parameter) and must hold for all its values, collect like powers (or like functions) of that parameter and set each coefficient to zero to obtain conditional equations determining the unknowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Porism formation: eliminate auxiliaries then equate coefficients of indeterminates
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate / from (5, 6), and then, since / is indeterminate, we have ...; hence, from (7,8) we get ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical porism solution procedure: form algebraic expressions for relevant segments/lines, eliminate auxiliary unknowns, then because some resulting symbol is indeterminate, equate its coefficients to zero to obtain the required relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain the double sign in algebraic expressions for lengths for generality; be consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: The double sign is essential to the general expression of that length. The one which we use as adapted to any specified case, merely for the sake of convenience, like the sign of direction in the co-ordinate axes, ought, however, when once adopted, to be adhered to throughout the entire investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When expressing directed lengths/perpendiculars algebraically, include ± ambiguity when the formulation has two symmetric possibilities. Choose a sign convention for a particular case and then keep it consistently through the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer line form y = x tan w ± b when dealing with perpendiculars
rubrics_metrics.description: The best form in which to take the equation of the straight line, when the lengths of perpendiculars upon it are to be considered, is y = x tan w ± b, as then the perpendicular from x1,y1 upon it, is most simply expressed, by p = (y1 − b) cos w − x1 sin w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt this form to obtain simple expressions for perpendicular distances in terms of cos w and sin w; this makes subsequent equating of coefficients in sin w and cos w straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equate coefficients of independent trig functions when identity in angle variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming now the equation of the porism, and equating to zero the co-efficients of the arbitraries sin w and cos w, we have ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an identity must hold for all values of an angular parameter w, expand into sin w and cos w components and equate their coefficients separately to obtain determining equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce arbitrary quantities (porismatising) to generalise expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: That whenever an algebraical expression is given, one or more arbitrary quantities may be introduced into the expression without altering its value. The process of finding the forms under which these arbitrary quantities appear, or of assigning the conditional equations, he calls porismatising the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Gompertz's principle to introduce auxiliary/parameter quantities to generalise or reparameterise expressions (including justifications for using imaginary symbols), then deduce the conditional equations that preserve the original value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect multiple (typically two) porismatic solutions in symmetric positions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are, hence, two points which fulfil the conditions of the porism, one in each of the opposite angles formed by the given straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When solving porisms with symmetric geometry, anticipate multiple roots/points (often two), typically lying in opposite sectors; algebraic solution should reveal these multiple values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose axes to obtain symmetrical results — several recommended choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods (3, 4, 5) give symmetrical results. (1.) Take the first and second given lines as axes of co-ordinates. (2.) Take the first line, and the line bisecting the angle formed by the other two, as axes. (3.) Take the lines bisecting the angles formed by the first and second, and by the second and third, as axes. (4.) Take the line bisecting the angle formed by these two last axes, and a perpendicular to it, as axes. (5.) Take the axes generally without regard to the given lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select among the listed axis choices depending on whether symmetry or simplicity is desired; choices (3–5) tend to produce more symmetrical formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify reality/positivity of parameters (porismatic ratio) algebraically
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, however, to shew the truth of the porism, necessary to prove that this value of f is always positive, or B always real. For sin 2w_i write its value 2 sin w_i cos w_i... then the numerator is identical with [sum of squared-like terms] and every term of this being essentially +-, the whole expression is essentially +-, and the value of f essentially real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After deriving a formula for a parameter (e.g., m or B), demonstrate it is real/positive by algebraic manipulation (e.g., expressing numerator as sum of squares or showing each term is positive) to ensure the geometric object exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symmetry: expect solutions expressible by symmetric functions of given parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherefore the point H is determined; and it is expressed, as we might expect, by symmetrical functions of m and n, and of b and c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When problem data are symmetric (e.g., ratios m,n or segments b,c), look for and present solutions in symmetric form — this both simplifies expressions and matches geometric intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form porism equation by expressing given condition algebraically and reduce by equating coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming the expression of the porism, and equating the co-efficients of to zero, we have ... B (p+q) cos K − a (pq) sin K = 0, (c+ b') (p+q) sin K − a' B = 0; from which ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate the verbal porism-condition (e.g., P.AD + Q.AE = 2') into an algebraic expression using the coordinate expressions for AD, AE etc., collect terms in arbitrary parameter(s) and equate coefficients to obtain determining equations.
